correctness.rationale: Parity linear algebra proves all graphs of degree at most three have an equilibrium. A universal-vertex strategy covers all remaining graphs through five vertices. Both displayed six-vertex examples have explicit no-equilibrium contradictions. A complete, executed enumeration of every connected labeled graph through six vertices, all action assignments, and all permutations of six labels found 300 failures exactly, partitioned into two canonical classes of 180 and 120. Finite enumeration is exhaustive only because its state space is explicitly bounded and traversed in full.

value.rationale: The 0-or-2 pattern is an explicitly named natural open case from the original 2022 paper; later general hardness proofs leave the first graph size and first graph topologies unresolved. The lower-order universal argument plus exact two-class minimal-obstruction census is a complete, motivated finite structural classification. It distinguishes minimal nonexistence structure from a general hardness proof; no claim of broad new algorithm or theorem for larger graphs is made.
